findings.desc: concept-cleanup: cross_host_review command calls submitLocalVerdict twice and emits host_verdict process events (L4 evidence-producing), but is missing entries in both command-policy.ts and process-fact-levels.ts — every other evidence-producing command (autopilot_review_submit, quorum_submit) has both entries; without a command-policy entry the access-control tier is undeclared

findings.desc: dispatch-policy: allowReviewOnlyRealHostSubprocess=true un-gates checkDispatchPolicy for codex but lattice-dispatch.ts line 2710 triggers runCodexRealLeafDispatch on allowRealHostSubprocess===true alone — a policy with both flags + allowedHosts=[codex] passes checkDispatchPolicy as authorized, then lattice-dispatch runs the IMPLEMENTATION path; the review-only narrowing is enforced only at the policy-check layer, not at the dispatch-execution layer, defeating the stated narrower-grant intent
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in ca7615450 (see commit body); smoke 21 checks green, tsc clean.

findings.desc: doc-promise-undelivered: handlers/cross-host-review.ts CrossHostReviewArgs.policy (line 26) and command-catalog description promise "Optional dispatch policy name governing the read-only Codex subprocess" but args.policy is never read or applied in the handler — the Codex subprocess runs unconditionally with no policy enforcement; the envDenylist, allowedPaths, maxRuntimeMinutes, and commandAllowlist from any supplied policy are silently ignored
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in ca7615450 (see commit body); smoke 21 checks green, tsc clean.

findings.desc: handlers/cross-host-review.ts line 287: jointDecision is called without the optional JointMaterialBinding parameter, leaving the materialHash-divergence guard in core/cross-host-review.ts unused in production; the leaf already fails closed on mismatch so this is defense-in-depth only, but the handler never passes hostAMaterialHash+hostBMaterialHash even though both are available (materialDigest and hostBVerdict.materialHash), and the feature is smoke-tested only at the direct pure-function level (CHK-002:adversarial:0), not through the handler
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in ca7615450 (see commit body); smoke 21 checks green, tsc clean.

findings.desc: dead-code: dispatch-policy.ts:447-448 reviewOnlyCodex is always false inside checkDispatchPolicy — the variable is computed as `allowReviewOnlyRealHostSubprocess===true && allowRealHostSubprocess!==true` but the entire enclosing block is `if (policyRecord.allowRealHostSubprocess===true)`, making the second operand permanently false. The variable is never true, so its only use at L451 (`!reviewOnlyCodex`) never fires. The surrounding comment correctly states codex must stay refused here regardless, so the behavior is intentional — but the dead variable misleads readers into thinking a review-only exemption exists within this branch. The dead variable should be removed and the filter simplified to `if (host===antigravity || host===gemini || host===codex) return true` (with a one-line comment referencing the mutual-exclusion invariant).
findings.resolvedReason: Removed dead reviewOnlyCodex var in checkDispatchPolicy; codex refused directly in the allowRealHostSubprocess block, carve-out lives in create/validate path (ecbce6853)

findings.desc: quality-cleanup: handlers/cross-host-review.ts:48 buildRedactedEnv empty-allowlist semantics undocumented and unsafe-by-default — when policy.envAllowlist is [] (the default from createDispatchPolicy and normalizeDispatchPolicyRecord), `allowlist.size>0` is false and the allowlist guard is completely bypassed, so every env var not matching UNSAFE_ENV_PATTERN passes through to the codex subprocess (e.g. DATABASE_URL, OPENAI_ORG_ID, GH_HOST, any non-standard secret names). The function comment says `ONLY those names may pass` but qualifies it with `If the policy declares an envAllowlist`, making the empty-allowlist=allow-all behavior a silent footgun. The fix is to document this explicitly in the function comment (e.g. `empty allowlist = allow-all minus denylist/pattern — this is intentional but callers should set an explicit allowlist for production use`) and ideally emit a warning or treat empty allowlist as deny-all for the review subprocess path, which is the higher-security default.
findings.resolvedReason: Broadened UNSAFE_ENV_PATTERN to catch DATABASE/DSN/CONNECTION/AUTH/SESSION/COOKIE/PRIVATE/ACCESS/*_URL/*_URI + documented empty-allowlist semantics (ecbce6853)

findings.desc: CHK-001:adversarial:2 through :5 are implemented as runtime smoke checks but are NOT registered as verificationIntents in the checklist and have no verificationEvidence. The smoke grew 17->21 but the checklist verificationIntent list still only declares 17 intents. The four new checks exercise real F-003/F-004 fix behaviors (codex BOTH-flags refused; missing policy fail-closed; unauthorized policy fail-closed; env-denylist+timeout threaded to runner) — each is non-hollow and non-tautological. They must be registered as verificationIntents (priority=must, category=adversarial) so the gate can verify the new fix behaviors are evidenced.

All 17 verificationEvidence records are stale: their materialHash binds to headHash e89b0aa54916b1cb8b26c84b84a0c27deb8dd304 (pre-fix baseline), but commit ca7615450 advanced the material hash. The validate gate reports 0/17 covered. The evidence records are non-hollow (they name specific smoke check labels, exact command, and specific assertions) but they must be re-stamped against the current materialHash after the fix commit for the REVIEW gate to consider them fresh.
findings.resolvedReason: Refreshed 21/21 verification evidence to current materialHash (6af70a7)

findings.desc: handlers/cross-host-review.ts lines 476-548 computes the HEAD materialDigest and performs assertMaterialCleanForReview only before spawning Codex, then records verdicts after runCodexReviewLeaf without isolating the tree or rechecking/locking material state. Because codex exec reviews the live mutable worktree and the leaf verdict merely echoes the requested materialHash, another local writer can modify source after the clean preflight but before or during the review; the recorded pass/fail is then bound to HEAD even though Codex reviewed transient uncommitted content. CHK-001:adversarial:6 only covers dirt present before spawn, not this TOCTOU window. Run Codex against an immutable clean snapshot/temp worktree at HEAD, or hold a source write lease and revalidate material state before recording.

cross_host_review accepts caller-supplied hostA/hostB identifiers but never fail-closed-validates that host A and host B remain independent. If a caller passes the same host id, the handler derives the same sessionId/keyId for both records and can still return jointDecision=pass when both decisions pass and findings agree. Downstream summarizeVerdicts collapses the shared identity, but the new cross_host_review proof surface itself can overstate an independent joint pass instead of stopping on non-independent reviewer identities. Mirror quorum_submit's hostId/sessionId/keyId independence guard before recording verdicts or computing jointDecision.
